note: Disclosure ledger for private and recently private payments companies (Stripe, Ramp, Brex, Airwallex, Checkout.com, Mercury, Rapyd, Nium): company-stated volumes, run rates, priced-round and tender valuations, statutory-account figures, and Capital One's purchase-price allocation for Brex. Each figure keeps its qualifier; press-only figures are kept as reported_talks rows and never charted.

rows.caveat: All money moved through Mercury accounts and cards, up 59% from 2024 per the company; a banking-flow measure, not acquiring TPV.
rows.curator_notes: Read 'Mercury transaction volume grew to $248B, up 59% from $156B in 2024.' under 'The numbers'. Dated 'February 5, 2026'.

rows.definition: Annual transaction volume for 2024, as stated by Mercury.
rows.source_name: Mercury via Business Wire: Series C release
rows.caveat: A banking-flow measure, not acquiring TPV; up 64% year over year per the company.
rows.curator_notes: Read '$156 billion in annual transaction volume, up 64% year-over-year' in the milestones list.

rows.definition: Revenue for calendar 2024 as stated by Mercury ('$500 million in revenue in 2024'); a full-year figure, not annualized.
rows.source_name: Mercury via Business Wire: Series C release
rows.caveat: Company-stated round number for full-year revenue, unaudited in the release. Full-year basis, so not directly comparable with annualized run rates.
rows.curator_notes: Read '$500 million in revenue in 2024' in the milestones list. metric_kind stated_run_rate is the closest company-stated revenue kind in the closed list.

rows.caveat: The round mixed primary and secondary funding. Superseded by the May 2026 Series D at $5.2 billion.

rows.definition: Customers choosing Mercury, as stated by the company (includes personal-banking users).

rows.caveat: A lower bound ('more than 300,000'); includes individuals using Mercury Personal, not only businesses.

rows.source_name: Nium via PR Newswire: Series E release

rows.definition: Net revenue for 2022 from Nium's audit, as stated in its release; a full-year figure, not annualized.
rows.source_name: Nium newsroom: 2022 net revenue release

rows.definition: Valuation in the round that financed the PayU GPO acquisition, as reported by Calcalist.
rows.source_name: Calcalist (Ctech): Rapyd raises $500M at $4.5B valuation to complete $610M PayU acquisition
rows.caveat: Press report ('Calcalist has learned'); Rapyd's own completion release names the investors but no valuation. Down from about $10 billion in 2021. Never charted.
rows.curator_notes: Read 'The company's valuation in this funding round was approximately $4.5 billion, down from the $10 billion valuation the company achieved in 2021.' Rapyd release (rapyd.net, 2025-03-14) read: no valuation stated.

rows.definition: Expected combined revenue after the PayU GPO acquisition, as reported by Calcalist.
rows.source_name: Calcalist (Ctech): Rapyd raises $500M at $4.5B valuation to complete $610M PayU acquisition
rows.caveat: Forward-looking press statement ('will ... generate revenues exceeding $1 billion'), not a company-reported result; basis (gross or net) unknown. Never charted.
rows.curator_notes: Read 'Following the acquisition, Rapyd will employ approximately 1,600 people and generate revenues exceeding $1 billion'.

gaps.why: Stripe does not publish group revenue or net revenue; only volume, tender valuations and product run rates. The page must bound it (e.g. take rate on volume), not state it.
FY2025 turnover, cost of sales and profit were read in RTE's report of the filed accounts; the Irish CRO filing itself was not opened, so those rows are left chartable false.

Full accounts to 31 Dec 2024 (filed 2025-10-02) and to 31 Dec 2025 (filed 2026-09-29) are Companies House PDFs that could not be read with the available tools. Checkout.com also says the UK entities cover only part of the group. Third-party aggregators of those accounts were not used.
Company releases give only growth rates (45% core growth in 2024, over 30% in 2025), no dollar figure for those years; the $750m figure is annualised as of September 2026.
Ramp has stated only 'over $1 billion' at every date since August 2025; Bloomberg's '$1.5 billion' is unconfirmed. No company-confirmed figure above the lower bound.

gaps.metric: revenue, card spend and deposit balances
gaps.why: Brex stopped stating revenue figures; Capital One reports Brex inside Domestic Card and does not disclose Brex revenue, purchase volume or partner-bank deposit balances separately. The purchase-price allocation is provisional as of 2026-06-30.
Latest company-stated figure is $650 million annualized as of Q3 2025, repeated unchanged in the May 2026 release.
Rapyd's own releases state none of these; only press reports (Calcalist) give a valuation and a forward revenue figure.

Nium disclosed only '50%+' revenue growth for 2023 and no later absolute revenue or volume figure in its own releases; a June 2026 interview gives only a fraction of a $1 billion target. A March 2026 '$3 billion pre-IPO round' story found in search could not be traced to Nium or a reputable outlet and was not used.
Airwallex states annualized revenue and volume only; no audited full-year revenue was found in company releases.
